newsitem.title: UK: N.Sea wet crudes trade steady to slightly easier.
newsitem.headline: N.Sea wet crudes trade steady to slightly easier.

text.p: North Sea physical crude markets traded unchanged to slightly weaker on Wednesday, continuing to reflecting ample June availabilities, traders said.
A cargo of Brent loading June 17-19 changed hands at July Brent -70 cents, unchanged from Tuesday when a cargo loading the same dates moved also at a 70 cent discount.
Other trades included a June 25-27 Draugen at Dated +10 cents and a June 27-29 Ekofisk sold weaker at Dated -1 cent.
About five Statfjords moved and while the values were not disclosed traders said they appeared to be in the range of Dated Brent -5 cents/+5 cents, unchanged to slightly weaker.
An Ekofisk loading July 1-3 changed hands at Dated -3 cents.
Most players saw the API stock data as broadly neutral. Market talk earlier was balanced between those expecting weaker differentials and those thinking Brent had hit bottom.
The only Brent cargo nominated loading dates of June 26-28 was kept ahead of the five o'clock deadline. Traders said the cargo was kept by Glencore. The equity holder was Shell.
The outright value of Brent was firmer. July IPE crude futures were 32 cents firmer at $17.82 a barrel at 1645 GMT. The August IPE futures contract was 32 firmer at $18.09.
The July/August intermonth was three cents to the good at -27/-26 cents and August/September was stronger at -21/-19 cents.
Next week's contracts for difference were slightly perkier at August Brent -68/-61 cents, with the folliowing week at August Brent -55/-50 cents.
